text:
noah: FYI I noticed streaming histograms weirdness during the live rollout of routing-update-4. spikes in 300-600ms buckets, but only for routes tagged with `canary=true`. anyone else?
maria: saw it too. spikes coincide with canary traffic and a handful of reconnect alerts. counts are small but visible on the latency heatmap.
aj: quick skim: our sampling code marks `telemetry.sample_rate` at request start (pre-routing). that means route-specific throttles/endpoints can shift actual forwarded events and produce misleading per-route metrics.
kevin: plus, the ingest pipeline has a short buffered window. when it gets saturated we observe `enqueue_ms` ~250-400 which pushes small reconnects into higher buckets. we need to surface that in console.
console-bot: FR created: #FR-2177 "Add ingest_enqueue_ms overlay + per-route sampling view on streaming histogram" (assigned eng-platform).
sre-bot: alert: reconnect-burst on route=chat-canary region=eu > 200 in 60s, auto-scaled.
lina: repro I used: run 20 clients with no jitter and a 900ms client retry. proxies were using 800ms grace on the canary edge. predictable overlap.
noah: that timing mismatch explains duplicate session starts and the bucket shift. but two separate problems: (1) sampling pre-routing causes misattribution, (2) ingest backlog amplifies apparent latency.
maria: UX request: add a small toggle on the histogram to show `sample_rate` over time (per-route when available) and annotate recent infra rollouts that touched proxy keepalive/coalescing so SREs can correlate.
aj: implementation note: moving sampling post-routing is safer for per-route accuracy but increases forwarded event volume to the ingest layer until it can decide. we could implement a lightweight pre-tag handshake: route selector emits a small "telemetry-tag" message to ingest with route and candidate id, ingest holds decision for a few ms and then applies sampling.
kevin: alternative: keep sampling where it is but attach `route_hint` to the sampled payload. That doesn't fully fix sample bias but gives analytics a way to reweight counts. downside: unsampled events have no route info.
lina: short-term mitigations: (A) increase ingest replicas for canary routes, (B) apply client-side jitter in canary SDK, (C) add billing debounce for session-starts with same session id within 2s to avoid double charges.
oah: agreed. also add `X-Trace-Session` header on session starts so we can trace a reconnect across routing -> proxy -> ingest -> billing. small header, big win for debugging.
maria: console-side: show `active_sessions` gauge, `session_starts` vs `unique_active` overlay, and expose recent rollout tags on the timeline. I can spec a mockup.
console-bot: ticket #UI-912 added for those UI changes.
aj: technical follow-up: i'll prototype a post-route sampling handshake using a minimal `route_tag` event and measure additional ingest QPS. if uplift is <15% we can consider moving sampling.
kevin: i'll add a runtime flag to annotate `ingest.enqueue_ms` in the telemetry pipeline so the histogram can surface it with little perf cost. also enabling debounce on billing for flagged routes.
lina: I'll pause the canary until we have SDK jitter PR merged or route sticky rule in place. canary rollback queued.
sre-bot: mitigation in place: sticky-routing enforced for `canary=true` and ingest replicas scaled +1 for 15m window.
oah: good short-term. long-term: robust parser and boundary-agnostic streaming paths, post-routing sampling, and clearer console overlays. let's track tasks in eng-platform board and sync next week.
maria: thanks all. leaving notes in rollout playbook: include keepalive/grace alignment test and a small reconnect-storm sim script.
